LLM01.name: Prompt Injection
LLM01.description: Input to the model - direct user input, retrieved content, tool output, image, audio or video content, intermediate reasoning, or persistent memory - alters the model's behavior in ways the developer did not intend. LLMs draw no architectural boundary between instructions and data.

LLM02.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
LLM02.description: An LLM-integrated system exposes confidential, regulated, privileged, or proprietary data through an unauthorized channel. Disclosure surfaces include the final answer, tool-call arguments, reasoning traces, retrieved chunks, logs, embeddings, and observable inference properties.

LLM03.name: Excessive Agency
LLM03.description: Damaging actions performed in response to unexpected, ambiguous, or manipulated model output, arising from excessive functionality, permissions, or autonomy granted to an LLM-based system.

LLM04.name: Supply Chain
LLM04.description: Vulnerabilities affecting the integrity of training data, models, adapters, conversion pipelines, and deployment platforms. Model artifacts, provenance, and conversion/merge workflows are first-class attack surfaces.

LLM05.name: Data and Model Poisoning
LLM05.description: An adversary or unsafe process manipulates data or model artifacts to embed harmful behavior, bias, or exploitable weaknesses - during pre-training, fine-tuning, embedding creation, retrieval augmentation, or model distribution.

LLM06.name: Unbounded Consumption
LLM06.description: An LLM application allows excessive and uncontrolled inferences, enabling denial of service, unsustainable financial cost, or model cloning. Defined by cost asymmetry: attackers trigger disproportionately expensive computation at negligible cost to themselves.

LLM07.name: Misinformation
LLM07.description: The model produces incorrect, incomplete, unsupported, or misleading information credible enough to influence a human decision, an automated workflow, or an agent action. A system-level failure when downstream components consume the incorrect output.

LLM08.name: Hidden Context Exposure
LLM08.description: Unauthorized extraction, inference, or reconstruction of hidden, non-user-facing system instructions or operational context - the system prompt, developer instructions, retrieved policy text, and tool/function schemas. Renamed and widened from 2025's System Prompt Leakage.

LLM09.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
LLM09.description: Weaknesses in how vectors and embeddings are generated, stored, or retrieved, exploiting the geometry of the embedding space and the mechanics of similarity search. Covers RAG, vector-backed agent memory, semantic caches, and deduplication pipelines.

LLM10.name: Improper Output Handling
LLM10.description: Insufficient validation, sanitization, and handling of model-generated output before it is passed to downstream components, enabling XSS, CSRF, SSRF, privilege escalation, or remote code execution. Now also spans insecure code generated by assistants at scale.
